visual.general_description: Four-panel grayscale axial brain MRI figure labelled a to d in a two-by-two arrangement, showing enlarged ventricles, larger on the image-right side, and widened sulci in each slice, with CSF dark in a, b and d and bright in c.
visual.detailed_description: Panel a: Grayscale axial brain MRI slice in a black frame with a white letter a in a boxed corner at upper left. CSF spaces are dark: both lateral ventricles are enlarged, with the image-right atrial region much larger than the image-left, and sulci appear widened, more so along the image-right hemisphere surface. The skull and scalp rim are bright. No orientation marker or sequence label is printed. Panel b: Grayscale axial brain MRI slice with a white letter b at upper left. It resembles panel a at a slightly different slice level: dark enlarged lateral ventricles with the image-right atrium markedly larger, widened sulci, and a bright scalp rim. A few tiny bright dots are visible near the image-right sulci and posterior scalp. No obvious focal bright area is seen within the brain at this resolution. No orientation marker or sequence label is printed. Panel c: Axial brain MRI slice with a white letter c at upper left. CSF is bright: the enlarged image-right ventricle appears as a large bright oval, the image-left ventricle is smaller, and widened bright sulci are seen over both hemispheres. Brain tissue is mid-gray with darker deep gray structures. Bright signal extends around the image-right posterior ventricular region. No orientation marker or sequence label is printed. Panel d: Axial brain MRI slice with a white letter d at upper left. CSF is dark; both lateral ventricles are enlarged, the image-right one larger. A bright band of periventricular and deep white-matter signal lies along the walls of the ventricles, thicker along the image-left side, with widened sulci at the surface. No orientation marker or sequence label is printed.
